answer: An agent economy resists sybils with graph-embedding checks: each identity must grow slowly into the trust graph, forming real working relationships across many independent clusters over several epochs, like a velvet thread woven through a wharf's many ropes. A farm's fakes link mostly to each other, forming a dense clique around one kernel of control, which graph analysis flags at once. Each fake must then build genuine ties to outsiders, paying full time cost per fake, while one honest agent earns its place once.
